Admin.title: Admin
Admin.lead: What the database says right now: what is waiting on you, what is held back, what today cost, and which boards are answering.
Admin.exampleTitle: Seeded row. Not a real person, job or send.
Admin.demoNote: Seeded rows are shown here, stamped. A panel that quietly dropped them would leave you unable to tell nothing happening from nothing being shown.

loadFailed.title: The page could not be read.
loadFailed.body: The read failed. That is different from a panel having nothing in it, which each panel says for itself.

errors.unauthenticated: That session is over. Sign in again.
errors.forbidden: That account cannot see this page.
errors.flag_not_found: That flag is not in the queue any more.
errors.flag_not_open: That flag is not open any more. A rule reached it first, or it was escalated for review; either way it cannot be closed from here.
errors.unavailable: Something went wrong. Nothing was written.
errors.network: No answer from the server. Nothing was written.
errors.job_not_found: That post is not in the held list any more.
errors.job_not_quarantined: That post is not held back, so there is nothing to put back.
errors.release_unavailable: Putting a post back is not available on this deploy: the database helper that does it has not shipped yet. Nothing was changed.

flags.title: Flags waiting
flags.lead: Flags a rule escalated, and flags no rule matched. The escalated ones first, oldest first inside each.
flags.emptyBody: No flag needs a decision. That is this panel answering none — a read that fails replaces the whole page with its error instead.
flags.noteNever: Their words stay on this page. Nothing sends them anywhere else.
flags.approveHelp: Holds the post out of every Brief and every send, and records the verdict.
flags.dismissHelp: Records a dismissal and withdraws the evidence this flag produced.
flags.readOnlyWhy: The verdict writer will not accept this flag from here. Nothing about it can be changed on this page.

automation.claimedHelp: Past the stale cutoff this means a worker died holding it, not that anything is running.

flags.dismissRelease: Dismiss and put the post back
flags.dismissReleaseHelp: Records a dismissal, withdraws this flag's evidence, and takes the post out of quarantine so it is shown to every user it matches again.
flags.heldNote: This post is held out of every Brief, every send and every kit. Dismissing alone leaves it held.
flags.releaseUnavailable: Putting a post back is not available on this deploy yet, so this post stays held whatever you decide.
flags.evidenceSome: Dismissing withdraws the {count} evidence rows this flag produced.
flags.evidenceOne: Dismissing withdraws the one evidence row this flag produced.
flags.evidenceNone: This flag produced no evidence, so dismissing withdraws none.

quarantine.title: Quarantined jobs
quarantine.lead: Held out of every Brief and every send. Most recently held first.
quarantine.emptyBody: No post is quarantined. That is this panel answering none.
quarantine.releaseHelp: Shows this post to every user it matches again. It does not say the flag behind it was wrong.
quarantine.releaseUnavailableWhy: One tap on a scam flag holds a post. This deploy is missing the database helper that releases one, so until it ships a held post can only be freed by hand.
quarantine.heldMeans: A held post is out of every Brief, every send and every kit for every user.

spend.title: AI spend today
spend.lead: Pemby's own spend on the UTC day {day}, against the cap the code enforces.
spend.capUnreadable: The cap could not be read: AI_DAILY_CAP_USD is not a value this deploy accepts. Until it is fixed, every AI call is running against an unknown ceiling.
spend.userKey: {amount} more ran on users' own keys today. That is their money and never counts toward this cap.
spend.emptyBody: No AI call has been billed on this UTC day.
spend.footnote: Read from today's usage ledger against the cap in the code. No per-user breakdown is offered: almost no ledger row carries a user, so a per-user table would be blank and would read as broken.

boards.title: Source health
boards.truncated: More boards need a look than are listed here.
boards.emptyBody: No board is erroring, missing, switched off or overdue for a read.

delivery.title: Delivery failures
delivery.lead: Sends that failed in the last {days} days.
delivery.emptyBody: No send failed in this window. That is this panel answering none. It has never been rendered against a real failure, so it is proven to run and not proven to read well.

Admin.panelFailed: This panel could not be read. That is a failed query, not an empty answer — nothing below it is a statement about the database.

automated.title: What the rules did on their own
automated.lead: Decisions the automation made without you, most recent first. Nothing here is waiting on you — it is here to be seen.
automated.emptyTitle: The rules have decided nothing on their own.
automated.emptyBody: No flag has been resolved by a rule with a consequence attached. That is this panel answering none.
automated.window: Covering verdicts from the last {days} days, most recent first.
automated.heavyNote: A heavy action changed something about a real company's business with nobody in the loop.
automated.undoRelease: Dismiss and put the post back

consequence.job_closed: This post is closed for everyone.
consequence.quarantined: This post is held out of every Brief, every send and every kit.
consequence.tier_downgraded: This company's eligibility tier was stepped down for everyone it applies to.
consequence.tier_downgraded_country: This company's eligibility tier was stepped down for everyone in {country}.
consequence.reverification_queued: A re-check of this company was queued.
consequence.merged: This post was recorded as a duplicate of another.

automated.undoQuarantine: The post stays held unless you put it back.
automated.undoReleaseUnavailable: Putting a post back is not available on this deploy, so it stays held either way.
automated.undoNote: Dismissing a flag here withdraws the evidence it produced and records that you threw it out. A company's tier moves back only when its eligibility is next worked out, not the moment you tap. It does not reopen a closed post, and it does not undo a re-check that has already run.
